topic: TRA-K far transfer: semantic distance, far transfer, schema-plus-retrieval

items.citation: Barnett, S. M. & Ceci, S. J. (2002). When and where do we apply what we learn? A taxonomy for far transfer. Psychological Bulletin, 128(4), 612-637.
items.claim: Far transfer varies along content and context dimensions; domain distance alone is not a sufficient predictor.

items.citation: Gick, M. L. & Holyoak, K. J. (1983). Schema induction and analogical transfer. Cognitive Psychology, 15, 1-38.
items.claim: Transfer between semantically disparate domains depends on an abstracted schema providing retrieval cues; schema quality predicts transfer.

items.citation: Gentner, D. (1983). Structure-mapping: A theoretical framework for analogy. Cognitive Science, 7(2), 155-170.
items.claim: Analogical mapping is relational, not attribute-based; a plausible surface overlap is not sufficient evidence for a transferred relation.

items.citation: Vendetti, M. S., Wu, A. & Holyoak, K. J. (2014). Far-Out Thinking: Generating solutions to distant analogies promotes relational thinking. Psychological Science, 25(4), 928-933.
items.claim: Generating solutions to semantically distant analogies, not near analogies, promoted relational transfer to an unrelated task.

items.citation: Tse, D. et al. (2007). Schemas and memory consolidation. Science, 316, 76-82.
items.claim: One-trial assimilation requires a previously established, consistent schema; inconsistent associations fail to assimilate rapidly.

items.citation: Nader, K., Schafe, G. E. & Le Doux, J. E. (2000). Fear memories require protein synthesis in the amygdala for reconsolidation after retrieval. Nature, 406, 722-726.
items.claim: Retrieval reopens a consolidated trace for update; computational analogue of supersession/demotion of an incumbent slot value.

items.citation: Tulving, E. & Thomson, D. M. (1973). Encoding specificity. Psychological Review, 80(5), 352-373.
items.claim: Retrieval depends on overlap with encoding operations; an overwritten or self-looped encoding leaves no effective cue.

items.citation: Johnson, M. K., Hashtroudi, S. & Lindsay, D. S. (1993). Source monitoring. Psychological Bulletin, 114(1), 3-28.
items.claim: Item familiarity and source credibility dissociate; a plausible low-credibility conflict should not displace a credible source by recency alone.
